headline: US and Japan intervene again? Yen appreciation nears 156 mark; Japanese analyst weighs in | International news | World
summary: The yen rose sharply against the dollar toward 156 as expectations grew for a Bank of Japan rate hike in September. Japan and the US announced intervention at the end of July.
why: The yen is a major funding and reserve currency, and its moves against the dollar affect Japanese exporters, carry trades and global FX positioning. Central-bank policy is the main driver of its value.
why_moved: Expectations of Bank of Japan tightening signals pushed the September rate-hike outlook higher, and the yen strengthened toward 156 per dollar. The input also cites US and Japanese intervention announced at the end of July.
